clue.text: Coward, for one, is unusually wary in predicament

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the synonym for predicament

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation or predicament

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of wary appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone timid is oddly cautious while stuck in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is Noel Coward, the English dramatist. AYWR (the anagram of WARY, from 'unusually') goes 'in' PLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward wrote stage comedies such as Private Lives, making him an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Check depth of water below fruit-tree, say

indicators.note: say signals the word sounds like the one wanted

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree

explanation.surface: Measure how deep the water is under an orchard tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' belongs to the definition, though it looks like a placement signal for the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound water with a weighted line to find its depth is to plumb it.

clue.text: Ship oars at sea, with male on board making brief observations

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so one piece goes into the other
at sea means confused, so the letters of ship oars are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man rows a vessel at sea while making pithy remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles SHIP OARS to APHORISS; 'on board' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a short pithy statement of a truth, a terse observation.

clue.text: Left outside in cacophony, play guitar or flute, perhaps

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes around the rest

parts.note: went means departed, left
taken as written
din is loud, harsh noise
to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: A musician walks out amid the noise, choosing guitar or flute.
explanation.walkthrough: WENT goes 'outside' IN + DIN + STRUM. 'guitar' belongs to the wordplay, not a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute is played by blowing, making it an example of a wind instrument.

clue.text: Country in which I come down to earth again?

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders in which nation they will touch down once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read 'I re-land', describing a second landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation in the British Isles, a country.

clue.text: Chap no longer doing well isn't entirely penniless, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is sounded, not spelled

parts.note: someone who has a bean has at least a little money

explanation.surface: A man down on his luck still has some money, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not having a bean' is British slang for being penniless, so having one means not being entirely broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A person past their prime whose success is over is a washed-up figure, the noun sense.

clue.text: Middleman oddly lacking intellectual product

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of Middleman leaves only its even-placed letters

explanation.surface: A go-between who strangely lacks any brainwork to show for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly lacking' removes letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of MIDDLEMAN, leaving I, D, E, A.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept is what the mind produces, a product of thought.

clue.text: Paper delivered in Irish house by end of day

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of day

explanation.surface: A newspaper delivered to the Irish parliament before the day is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper published every day is commonly called a daily paper.

clue.text: Guns badly positioned in vital vessel

indicators.note: positioned in means placed within the second word

parts.note: an artery is a major blood vessel
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Weapons poorly placed in an important ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a ship, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Large mounted guns, such as cannons, are collectively artillery.

clue.text: In rueful tone, be phoned about one unknown after a game

indicators.note: after means these pieces follow a game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: about means the phrase goes around the numeral

parts.note: to get a call is to be phoned
I is the Roman numeral one
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone takes a call after a match and sounds sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the phrase round the numeral rather than meaning 'concerning'; 'after' signals that everything else follows the opening article and sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in a rueful tone means expressing regret, which is how one speaks when saying sorry.

clue.text: Starts off fun thing we turn crazy

indicators.note: the starts of each of the three words fun, thing and we are taken off

explanation.surface: A light-hearted activity that we begin ends up driving us mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' removes the first letters F, T and W, leaving UN, HING and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange someone's mind is to make them go mad, a verb matching turn crazy.

clue.text: That fellow's in wrong post — unsound philosopher

indicators.note: in places the possessive inside the shuffled word
wrong signals the letters of post are put in the wrong order

parts.note: his is the possessive meaning that fellow's

explanation.surface: A man finds himself in the wrong job, a thinker whose reasoning does not hold up.
explanation.walkthrough: HIS goes 'in' SOPT, the anagram of POST from 'wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophist uses clever but fallacious arguments, so is a thinker whose reasoning is specious.

clue.text: Obstacle bounder put in the way of 1 ac

indicators.note: put in signals one word is placed inside another

parts.note: the clue at 1 across defines a dramatist, and J. M. Barrie, author of Peter Pan, was one
a cad is an ungentlemanly man, a bounder

explanation.surface: A cad is set up as a hindrance to the dramatist from the first clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to the answer of 1 across, a dramatist; here it is a specific one, Barrie, rather than the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier built across a street to block passage is an obstruction.

clue.text: Set down Circle Line going West? True

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means read from right to left

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A question about whether a London Underground route heads westward, answered yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going West' reverses LAY + O + L. The Circle Line is a London Underground route.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful and steadfast are senses shared by true and the answer, as in a true friend.

clue.text: Book, in current state, providing foundation

parts.note: as is means in the present condition, unchanged

explanation.surface: A book in its present condition serves as the groundwork for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the underlying support or starting point on which something rests.

clue.text: Daughter is set up in improved accommodation

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the synonym for improved

parts.note: better means improved

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A daughter is installed in better lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses IS to SI; D + SI goes 'in' BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsitter is a British one-room flat for living and sleeping, a type of lodging.

clue.text: Study I shred and disparage

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
to grate food is to shred it

explanation.surface: Someone in their study tears up papers and belittles them.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to belittle or speak critically of, a synonym of disparage.

clue.text: Like someone concealing one negative comment

parts.note: as means like, as in as before

indicators.note: concealing means the word for someone hides the numeral inside it

parts.note: a person is someone
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Similar to a person hiding one critical remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a disparaging remark attacking someone's reputation.

clue.text: Reported what was done about second copy

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the others

parts.note: a deed is an act, something that was done
to crib is to copy another's work

explanation.surface: An account given of the business of copying for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: DEED goes 'about' S + CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe events is to give an account of them, so reported is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Bishop left unconscious in error

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
under means anaesthetised, unconscious

explanation.surface: A churchman left senseless in a state of mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless or stupid mistake is a blunder, a synonym for error.

clue.text: Did as badly, in no respect

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of did as are put together in a poor order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone performed poorly, without any regard at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal on 'Did as', making DISDA; 'no respect' reads as a noun here, not as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is the lack of regard that the definition describes.

clue.text: What barmen like: last of brandy getting drunk

parts.note: bar staff are pleased to receive gratuities, or tips

indicators.note: last of picks out only the final letter of brandy

explanation.surface: Bar staff enjoy the final drop of brandy and end up intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly intoxicated, a milder synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Man led by instinctive force, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: led by places the second piece in front of the first

parts.note: the id is the Freudian name for the instinctive part of the psyche
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man driven by gut instinct, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic expression or turn of phrase, a way of speaking.

clue.text: Maiden seized by villain — mature monarch, for example

indicators.note: seized by means held inside the villain's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is captured by a scoundrel, and a grown-up king appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch' is the butterfly, not a king.

clue.text: Still having complaint about wings in side, liable to come off

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: an illness that is uncured is one still had

clue.text: MI5 or MI6, but not CIA, has one such piece of data

parts.words: MI5 or MI6, but not CIA, has one such piece of data
parts.note: MI5 and MI6 each include a number, 5 or 6, while CIA is letters only

clue.text: Worked out and, after short time, showered

clue.text: Getting together finally in group? Not entirely

clue.text: Cheat man in marginalised position, initially

definitions.meaning: to swindle or con someone out of money
a chess piece that starts the game in a corner square, at the edge of the board

clue.text: Poor connection giving relative tricky problem
